 Live .  17,880 viewing 17880 viewing Live page Updated 9 minutes ago Putin says Russia, US, and China share 'joint responsibility' for global peace
 Trump, Xi and Putin set to Hold Historic Meeting on Apec Sidelines
 BBC News
 Close Watch live Summary
 Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping have held talks in the Chinese city of Shenzhen - they lasted around 90 minutes 
 As the meeting began, Xi said the talks had "groundbreaking significance" - Trump said they were "really making history" 
 Meanwhile, Putin said Russia, China, and the US share a "joint responsibility" for "maintaining international peace and security" 
 This meeting would have been unthinkable not so long ago, writes our correspondent Nada Tawfik from the summit 
 Earlier, Trump held separate, bilateral meetings with Putin and Xi . He called Putin his friend - watch the moment here 
 After meeting Xi, Trump said the US and China want to see an end to the Ukraine war 
 There is growing frustration in many European circles that Xi does not put more pressure on Russia over Ukraine, writes Laura Bicker . For Putin, the summit is already seen as a diplomatic victory, says Steve Rosenberg

 Live Reporting
 Edited by Rorey Bosotti, with Laura Bicker, Steve Rosenberg, Nada Tawfik and Stephen McDonell in Shenzhen, China
 US team departs Kylin Villa published at 10:14 GMT 10:14 GMT 
 We've now received a report from the press pool reporter in Shenzen that the US motorcade has departed the Kylin Villa, where the trilateral meeting was taking place.
 President Trump is expected to return to the US in the coming hours.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 What did the three leaders say to kick off the meeting ? published at 10:11 GMT 10:11 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters President XI has said the meeting is the first of its kind in history and is of "groundbreaking significance" . 
 He added that the three countries should work together to address global challenges and "set an example" for the rest of the world.
 President Trump echoed Xi's sentiments saying the trilateral meeting is "really making history" and that the trio have a "special responsibility" to maintain productive dialogue. 
 He added: “No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for
engagement.”
 President Putin's contribution was similarly phrased as he emphasised how the three have a responsibility to preserve international peace. 
 He says Russia, China and the United States can strengthen global stability if they co-operate constructively. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Trilateral meeting concludes - media reports published at 10:01 GMT 10:01 GMT Breaking 
 The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin has concluded according to Chinese state broadcaster CCTV and Russian news agency Tass.
 In its report, Tass adds that the summit between the three leaders lasted an hour and a half.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 More details emerge from China's take on Xi Trump talks published at 09:58 GMT 09:58 GMT 
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images Xinhua, the state news agency of the People's Republic of China, has released its account of the bilateral meeting between President Trump and President Xi. 
 We reported earlier that Xi believes the latest talks have given the China-US relationship "new substance" - a view highlighted in the Xinhua report which says the two nations have explored the right way for two major powers to coexist defined by the principles of "respect, fairness, and reciprocity." 
 Xi says he hopes to continue steering the course of China-US relations alongside Trump, ensuring that this "great ship" remains on the right track as it sails forward.
 On the issue of Taiwan , the report says Washington should continue to do the right thing to avoid any major setbacks in China-US relations. 
 In terms of trade, there is a desire to see "mutual benefits" and on the subject of AI a desire for both countries to work to address security risks and keep AI under human control.
 The account says the two sides viewed this meeting as positive and constructive.

 Trump's critics argue he's unlikely to be firm in these meetings published at 09:42 GMT 09:42 GMT 
 Nada Tawfik 
North America correspondent reporting from Shenzhen, China 
 Image source, EPA There is an ongoing debate in US foreign policy circles,
reignited by this trilateral meeting, about whether US presidents should first
get clear commitments before meeting with adversaries at summits. 
 President
Trump’s critics have argued that he’s unlikely to be firm in these meetings,
given how effusive he’s been about his rapport with Xi and Putin. Based on what we’ve seen, it’s hard to argue against that.
 So far, we haven’t heard about concerns
expressed by US officials on things like getting more rare earths from China. 
 Before his bilateral meeting with President Xi, he painted the US-China relationship as a
fantastic one. Tariffs? Split up in a "very fair" way, he said. American
farmers had done "very well", with the president only lightly urging China’s
leader "to do some more for our farmers" by expanding agricultural purchases. 
 Trump believes their "very special relationship", as he called it, is the
best way to get results. "I think as long as you and I are in charge of things,
we’ll never have a problem."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Russia sees trilateral meeting as 'Yalta 2.0' published at 09:35 GMT 09:35 GMT 
 Liza Fokht 
BBC News Russian 
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images Vladimir Putin's opening remarks suggest that, in
a sense, Russia really does see today's meeting as a kind of "Yalta 2.0". 
 As a reminder, the original Yalta conference saw the leaders of the US, UK and Soviet Union meeting in the Crimean city in 1945 to discuss the post-war reorganisation of Europe 
 In his speech, Putin stressed that Russia, China
and the US were among the victorious powers in World War Two.
 He said the three countries share a "joint
responsibility" for "maintaining international peace and
security".
 The Russian president proposed discussing issues
such as global and regional economic, food and energy security, as well as the
resolution of regional conflicts - including the war in Ukraine.
 Putin also mentioned that he had already discussed
the war in Ukraine during his bilateral meetings with Xi and Trump.

 Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic talks - in pictures published at 09:26 GMT 09:26 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters Image caption, The three leaders walk together at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen
 Image source, Reuters Image caption, Trilateral talks take place around a very large table
 Image source, Reuters Image caption, Trump described the meeting as "really making history", Xi called "positive interaction" between major powers "a mandatory requirement", and Putin called for constructive co-operation
 Image source, Reuters Image caption, The leaders' comments are being closely scrutinised by the media

 Trump has given Putin a platform and praise published at 09:19 GMT 09:19 GMT 
 Nada Tawfik 
North America correspondent 
 Image source, AFP via Getty Images While Ukraine and the Europeans were hoping that Russia’s
invasion of Ukraine wouldn’t be discussed without them at this trilateral,
President Trump confirmed in his remarks that it most definitely will be. 
 And
not only that - he called it “the war between Russia and Ukraine,” blurring
Moscow’s role as aggressor.
 Key to understanding why President Trump seems to
continually give President Putin a pass on his war on Ukraine is that it didn’t
happen under his presidency. 
 In fact, Donald Trump continually claims that it
wouldn’t have happened if he were president instead of Joe Biden. 
 The US president has offered President Putin this major global platform of a
superpower, and he’s also been extremely praiseworthy. 
 He’s affectionately
referring to him as “Vladimir,” and “my friend,” and the body language has been
just as warm.

 'We're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon,' says Trump published at 09:12 GMT 09:12 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images We can now bring you more from US President Donald Trump's brief speech at the top of the trilateral meeting. 
 He references the three countries' nuclear capabilities, and says they are "uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth". 
 It is "vital" that they cooperate to "combat the threat of nuclear proliferation in other countries around the world", he says, adding: "That's what we're doing in Iran."
 "We're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon".
 Trump then turns to Ukraine, and says he and Putin have had a "long discussion" on the conflict there already.
 He says he thinks that Putin "and I hope the other side, would like to see an end to that war".
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Xi, Trump and Putin posed for photo before meeting published at 09:08 GMT 09:08 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Before the meeting began, Trump, Xi and Putin assembled on a stage in front of a blue backdrop with the words "China-Russia-US Shenzhen Summit" in three languages - Chinese, Russian, then English.
 The three countries' flags were arranged on stage, a set on each side of the leaders. Xi stood in the centre, with Trump to his left and Putin to his right.
 The trio left a minute later and proceeded into the hall where they would hold their trilateral meeting.

 Putin says much attention paid to Ukraine conflict during Apec published at 09:05 GMT 09:05 GMT 
 The Tass news agency is reporting more of Putin's comments during his trilateral meeting with Trump and Xi.
 He says the task of strengthening the system of international law rests on Russia, China, and the US as the founding members of the UN.
 Putin also notes that the three countries share many common interests in resolving regional conflicts, including the Ukrainian one.
 He says, at the initiative of Trump, much attention was paid to the Ukrainian conflict and all the countries have a shared interest to resolve it.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Putin calls for constructive co-operation published at 08:58 GMT 08:58 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Russia, China and the United
States can strengthen global stability if they co-operate
constructively, says President Vladimir Putin.
 He says Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President
Donald Trump should discuss global and regional issues as well
as energy security. 
 The Tass news agency reports that Putin believes the three countries are united not only by their status as victorious countries in World War II, but also by their responsibility for maintaining international peace.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Positive interaction among major powers not a matter of choice' - Xi published at 08:54 GMT 08:54 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Before giving the floor to his fellow leaders, Xi said that "positive interaction among major powers is not a matter of choice, but a mandatory requirement".
 Citing China as an example, he says Beijing has "advanced its comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination with Russia for a new era" and that it has "actively sought to build a constructive and strategically stable relationship" with the United States.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement,' says Trump published at 08:52 GMT 08:52 GMT 
 The US president says he, Putin and Xi have a "great deal to discuss", adding that they have "already discussed a lot".
 He says as the presidents of the three of the world's largest countries, they have a "special responsibility" to maintain productive dialogue. 
 "Too often past leaders have avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements," he says, adding: "We feel the opposite."
 He adds: "No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement and speech."
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Trilateral meeting 'really making history' - Trump published at 08:49 GMT 08:49 GMT Breaking 
 Donald Trump thanks China's President Xi for welcoming him "so warmly" back to China, calling it an "honour" to be there.
 He congratulates him on a "very successful Apec summit".
 He says he's "delighted" that it's given the opportunity for the first ever trilateral meeting between the US, China and Russia, saying they are "really making history".
 The meeting is still under way. We'll bring you more from it shortly. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Major powers bear 'special responsibilities' in today's 'global village' - Xi published at 08:46 GMT 08:46 GMT 
 The world today is "no longer a collection of isolated islands", Xi says.
 "Humanity lives in a single 'global village' where everyone’s fortunes are interconnected," he says, adding that major powers bear "special responsibilities" in this "global village".
 China has in recent years been promoting a form of major-power relations "characterised by peaceful coexistence, overall stability, and balanced development... that benefit the parties involved and the world at large", the Chinese president says.
 He urged China, Russia and the US to "set an example" for the rest of the world, by cooperating to address global challenges and facilitating peace and stability.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 China, Russia and US should 'learn from history' and 'work together', Xi says published at 08:40 GMT 08:40 GMT 
 Image source, Reuters We're getting more comments from Xi, who stresses how the three countries should "work together to address global challenges".
 "We should learn from history," he says, according to Reuters. "Adversity reveals true responsibility."

 Xi says three-way talks of 'groundbreaking significance' - local media published at 08:37 GMT 08:37 GMT 
 Image source, EPA Xi started the meeting by highlighting how the gathering of the leaders of China, Russia, and the United States - the first of its kind in history - is of "groundbreaking significance", China's Xinhua news agency reports.

 Will everyone at the trilateral meeting stick to the script? published at 08:35 GMT 08:35 GMT 
 Laura Bicker 
China correspondent, reporting from Shenzhen 
 Xi will want to control the optics of this meeting, from start to finish.
 Chinese officials like to nail down agendas with talking points and produce carefully choreographed speeches.
 But in this unprecedented summit, Xi will have to live with two very unpredictable leaders.
 Both Trump and Putin have their own agendas and the US president has already threatened to go off script.
 There is a risk that they both dominate the meeting and Xi ends up looking like a host, rather than the architect of a major diplomatic moment.
 Of course, Xi may be ready for this. It may even play into his hands.
 The Chinese leader has been trying to portray himself as a stable global leader - at this summit he will be flanked by two men embroiled in wars they cannot seem to end.
 So any unscripted moment could serve to highlight his preferred role as senior statesman.
 Read more of Laura's analysis here 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 This was unthinkable not so long ago published at 08:32 GMT 08:32 GMT 
 Nada Tawfik 
North America correspondent 
 Image source, EPA It wasn’t that long ago that a moment like this seemed unthinkable. 
 The fact that this is happening now speaks to this moment in geopolitics – but more importantly to the personalities and dynamics of these three leaders. 
 They have looked like old friends, rather than rivals, in their engagements here.
 But beyond the niceties, the reality is these three men have very different goals and motivations for this sit-down. That’s why many doubt there will be any major breakthroughs.
 But that doesn’t mean what is said here won’t potentially influence foreign policy, particularly when it comes to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
 President Trump boasts of his personal relationship with Xi and Putin and admires their grip on power. It’s something that has unsettled Washington’s allies.
 In an uncertain world, the big question now is whether this trilateral format outlasts the current US president.
